A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoChat-Flash and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary material. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison throughout; supplementary pages 13–17 are visually identical.

before.justification: v3 reports original VideoChat-Flash benchmark evaluations, NIAH experiments, ablations, efficiency measurements, and supplementary quantitative and qualitative results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Table 1 benchmark scores, Figure 5 NIAH results, and the appendix experiments and case studies.

M1.justification: The HiCo procedure, duration-based sampling, timestamp prompt, clip compression, progressive visual dropout, and four-stage training scheme are unchanged. No method component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training corpora and LongVid tasks. Coverage remains identical across Table 1's video benchmarks, single- and multi-hop NIAH, appendix MMMU/MME evaluations, and short-video, surveillance, and movie case studies.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables, encoder/connector and efficiency comparisons, and appendix comparisons. In particular, both NIAH evaluations retain LongVA and LLaMA-VID as baselines.

E3.justification: Reported frame sampling, clip/token budgets, model sizes and resolutions, training settings, evaluation metrics, and efficiency-estimation procedures match. Passages describing existing protocols move across pages without revisions.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same design, sampling, encoder/connector, and dropout ablations. Section 6.1's layer and attention analyses and Figures 11–14's qualitative case studies are also unchanged.

E5.justification: The statistical reporting practice is unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seed details, confidence intervals, or significance tests; both retain the same point estimates and plotted curves.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative outputs match. Examples retained in both include 74.0 MVBench accuracy for the 7B@448 model in Table 1, 99.1% single-hop NIAH accuracy at 10,000 frames in Figure 5, and MMMU 45.2/MME 1843.4 in Section 6.3.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), defining sampling, sampling density, clip encoding, and token concatenation, are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning HiCo compression, LongVid, short-to-long learning, multi-hop NIAH, and VideoChat-Flash's performance. Their scientific scope and strength do not change.

C2.justification: Interpretations of visual redundancy, shallow versus deep attention, dropout benefits, and multi-hop benchmark difficulty are unchanged. Existing qualifications, including Q-Former convergence difficulties in Section 7.1, remain without new limitations or explanations.

D1.justification: Implementation details, training hyperparameters, data-construction instructions, hardware and efficiency-measurement information, and the code-access link are unchanged. Sections 7–8 and Table 8 are identical.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 73 works and retain the same research positioning. Changed citation-location page numbers in the bibliography reflect pagination changes, not added or removed references.

P1.justification: v4 adds Shanghai Innovation Institute as an additional affiliation for Yi Wang and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose and section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation block accompanies text and float reflow. Figure 7 shifts downward, and Table 4 moves from the left to the right column on page 8, shifting Tables 5–6. Figure/table content, captions, and styling are retained; the supplementary pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v4 adds an author affiliation and reflows the main document while preserving the scientific text, results, references, and complete supplementary material. These administrative and layout changes produce no meaningful net difference in the paper's scientific support, reproducibility, or readability.
